original_question: Among degree-k polynomial threshold functions f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1}, is the one with maximal total influence always the symmetric threshold f(x) = sgn(p(x_1 + ... + x_n)), where p is a degree-k univariate polynomial alternating sign on the k+1 values of x_1 + ... + x_n closest to 0?
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting the named open problem 'Gotsman-Linial Conjecture' in arXiv:1204.6447; this paper has no numbered Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3, so the nearest official formulation is that exact named item.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's official statement, almost verbatim. It has the right function class (degree-k polynomial threshold functions on {-1,1}^n), the right extremal quantity (maximal total influence), and the right conjectured extremizer (a symmetric threshold of the form sgn(p(x_1+...+x_n)) with p alternating sign on the central k+1 values).
missing_details: The paper's statement is implicitly quantified over both n and k; a stand-alone version should say explicitly 'for every n >= 1 and k >= 1' or 'for fixed n and k'.

The note does not restate the definition of a degree-k polynomial threshold function, so a stand-alone version should specify that f(x) = sgn(Q(x)) for some real polynomial Q on the Boolean cube (standard convention: degree at most k, usually taken multilinear on {-1,1}^n).
The paper does not define total influence in this entry, so a stand-alone version should state I[f] = sum_{i=1}^n Pr_x[f(x) != f(x with the i-th coordinate flipped)].
A stand-alone formulation should address the sign-at-zero issue, e.g. by requiring the representing polynomial to be nonzero on all cube points, since otherwise sgn(Q(x)) is ambiguous.
The phrase 'the k+1 values of x_1+...+x_n closest to 0' should be made explicit as the attainable values of S_n = x_1+...+x_n on {-1,1}^n, i.e. the middle Hamming layers.

Your wording can be read as asserting uniqueness ('the one with maximal total influence'); the paper only states that the extremal maximizer is a symmetric one, so a sharper stand-alone version should ask whether the maximum is attained by such a symmetric PTF.

The paper separates this main extremal conjecture from weaker neighboring questions (the O(k) sqrt(n) and O_k(1) sqrt(n) influence bounds), so the refined question should keep the exact extremal statement and not fold in those weaker variants.
refined_question:
For every n >= 1 and k >= 1, let f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} range over all degree-k polynomial threshold functions, in the standard sense that f(x) = sgn(Q(x)) for some real multilinear polynomial Q of degree at most k with Q(x) != 0 for all x in {-1,1}^n. Must the maximum possible total influence
I[f] = sum_{i=1}^n Pr_x[f(x) != f(x_1,...,-x_i,...,x_n)]
be attained by a symmetric function depending only on S_n = x_1 + ... + x_n, namely by a function of the form f(x) = sgn(p(S_n)) where p is a real univariate polynomial of degree k whose sign alternates on the k+1 attainable values of S_n closest to 0?
justification: The nearest official formulation in arXiv:1204.6447 is exactly the named item 'Gotsman-Linial Conjecture', stated as an extremal problem for total influence among degree-k PTFs with the conjectured optimizer given by the same symmetric threshold form. The surrounding bullets show that the paper treats the O(k) sqrt(n) and O_k(1) sqrt(n) bounds only as weaker neighboring versions, so the draft is aiming at the full extremal conjecture, not those relaxations. Because this short note explicitly defers notation and definitions to an external reference rather than restating them, I kept the conjecture unchanged in substance but made explicit the hidden conventions needed for a self-contained research question: quantifiers over n and k, the real-polynomial PTF representation, the definition of total influence, the nonvanishing/sign issue, and the meaning of the 'values closest to 0' as the middle attainable sums on the Boolean cube.
